name: tee
summary: Writes its input both to a file and to the screen.
description: Like a T-fitting on a pipe: tee reads standard input, writes it to one or more files and also passes it on to standard output. It lets you keep a record of a command while seeing the result, or write to a protected file with sudo tee (sudo does not apply to a > redirection).

options.description: Appends to the end of the files instead of overwriting them.

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: File(s) to copy the input to.

examples.explanation: Shows the build and saves it to build.log.
Adds a line to a protected system file.
Saves the list to a file and counts the lines at the same time.
Writes to two files without showing anything.

dangerNote: Without -a, tee overwrites the contents of the target files. With sudo tee, a wrong path can replace a system file.
